items.title: Well-conditioned RGO update: finite variance and contraction

source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. ASTIS restatement, expanded mathematical proof and Lean formalization; no author endorsement implied.

items.statement: At a recursive stage let 0<η≤c₀<1/4. The well-conditioned branch κ_A<2 selects τ=c₀ and a=(η+c₀)/(1+A⁻¹), with A∈(0,∞]. The update (A⁺)⁻¹=A⁻¹+a⁻¹ has A⁺≤2c₀. For a finite previous A, it also satisfies A⁺≤ρ₀A, where ρ₀=2c₀/(1+2c₀)<1. These are the one-step parameter claims of Lemma 6.6(ii), not the later multi-stage algorithm theorem. ASTIS uses r=A⁻¹≥0 and proves A⁺>0 even at r=0. This selected scalar formula does not require c₀<1/4; that generalization is disclosed separately.
assumptions: r≥0 is precision. A previous finite regularization variance equals 1/r only when r>0; r=0 models A=∞ without using Lean's real inverse of zero as infinity.
0<h≤c implies c>0. The source restriction c<1/4 is not needed for this selected scalar branch.
The well-conditioned branch has already selected τ=c. This theorem does not test its condition number, prove branch persistence or implement a recursive sampler.
All quantities here are real scalar parameters, not random variables or the covariance of the Gibbs distribution. No measure-theoretic hypothesis is needed for the scalar inequalities.

obligations.label: Positive finite updated parameter bounded by twice the schedule constant, including initial infinity
Exact contraction factor for a positive previous precision

bindings.boundary: Only the deterministic well-conditioned parameter step of Lemma6.6(ii). The source condition-number test selects tau=c; it is not asserted by this lemma. c<1/4 is unnecessary for this scalar branch and explicitly generalized away. r^-1 represents a previous finite variance only under r>0. No finite-stage termination, implemented recursion, probability error, mixing or query cost. One-step regularization-parameter control is not a covariance estimate, a termination theorem, an error guarantee or an expected query-cost estimate.

assumption_deltas.lean: r≥0; updated precision positive; comparison with r⁻¹ guarded by r>0
assumption_deltas.reason: Zero precision retains the infinite initial case. A⁺=h+c there; no totalized real inverse of zero represents infinity.
The upper restriction c<1/4 is unused in this scalar branch and is not needed for 0<ρ<1.
No condition-number test, branch persistence or full recursive process is claimed.
